verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — Capitulation Near $60K, but No Catalyst Until CPI; AI Is Draining Crypto
verdict.rationale_short: Bitcoin is nearing $60,000 and Ethereum is approaching $1,700 after a brutal week that took the total crypto market cap down roughly 48% from its peak. The damage is macro, not crypto-specific: Friday's hot 172K jobs print pushed the 30Y back above 5.0% and delayed Fed-cut hopes, the US-Iran conflict is feeding the inflation fear, and capital is rotating from BTC into AI equities. Forced selling compounded it — a disclosed Strategy (MicroStrategy) bitcoin sale, >$3.2B in spot-ETF outflows, ~$7B in liquidations, and a Mt. Gox wallet transfer. STEP ASIDE at medium conviction: the weekend's ~$59,227 BTC low looks like capitulation, but there is no catalyst to buy before May CPI on June 10, and a hot print would confirm higher-for-longer and break $59K. The first technical signal worth respecting is an ETH reclaim of ~$1,674; until then, this is a knife, not a dip.

Friday's NFP printed 172K vs 85K consensus, breaking the equity framework (SPX -2.64% to 7,383.74, VIX ~20.9, 30Y back above 5.0%); crypto fell hardest as the highest-beta risk asset
Over the weekend BTC bottomed near ~$59,227 before steadying; ETH broke below $1,900 (down ~11% on the week); roughly $390B in crypto value was erased and ~$7B in leveraged positions liquidated

Forced-selling overhang: a disclosed Strategy (MicroStrategy) bitcoin sale, more than $3.2B in spot-BTC-ETF outflows, and a large Mt. Gox wallet transfer — supply hitting a market with no fundamental anchor
Constructive technical tell: a reclaim of resistance near $1,674 could start an ETH recovery phase; the long-term ETH outlook remains constructive, but a near-term catalyst is absent before CPI
Next macro binary: May CPI on June 10 (consensus near 4.2% YoY headline) ahead of the Warsh FOMC June 16-17 — the print that decides whether the rate regime that broke crypto eases or hardens

~$1,700 — broke below $1,900, down ~11% on the week; higher-beta than BTC. The first technical signal is a reclaim of ~$1,674; below it, $1,500 is the next major support.

trade_setups.thesis: Crypto fell ~48% from its peak on a macro break it cannot fight: higher yields, a firm dollar, delayed Fed cuts, and forced selling. With CPI June 10 the next catalyst and no fundamental anchor under price, the highest-expectancy posture is sidelined capital, ready to deploy on confirmation.
trade_setups.entry: Hold cash/stables; deploy only after CPI with VIX below 18 and BTC reclaiming $66,000
trade_setups.invalidation: A cool CPI + BTC reclaim of $66,000 reopens a starter long

trade_setups.thesis: ETH near $1,700 is washed out (-11% on the week) and a reclaim of the ~$1,674 resistance is the cleanest technical trigger for a recovery phase; the long-term platform thesis is intact. This is a level-defined starter, not a conviction add, given the hostile macro.
trade_setups.entry: Starter only on a daily close back above $1,674 with BTC holding $59K; add on $1,750 reclaim
trade_setups.invalidation: Daily close below $1,620 — stand aside; $1,500 is the next support

trade_setups.thesis: BTC's break of its store-of-value bid while the dollar rose confirms it is trading as high-beta risk, not a haven. Until the macro regime turns, rallies are to be faded near resistance rather than chased.
trade_setups.entry: No long below $66,000; treat $66-68K as resistance to fade if reached before CPI
trade_setups.invalidation: Two daily closes above $66,000 on falling VIX flips the near-term bias constructive

bear_case: The uncomfortable truth in a ~48%-from-peak drawdown is that crypto has no fundamentals to defend the price — it is pure supply, demand, and narrative, and all three turned at once. The macro that broke it (a hot labor market, the 30Y back above 5.0%, an Iran conflict feeding inflation and delaying Fed cuts) is not resolved, and the supply shock is structural: the largest corporate holder is selling, spot-ETF outflows exceed $3.2B, and a Mt. Gox transfer hangs over the bid. Capital is actively rotating out of bitcoin into AI equities, so even a risk-on bounce may not accrue to crypto. Invalidation level: a hot May CPI on June 10 with the 30Y above 5.05% breaks BTC's $59K capitulation low and targets $52-55K; only a cool CPI with BTC reclaiming $66,000 and VIX below 18 restores a constructive setup.
